messages:
mira: Morning — automated restore for tenant-77 failed during decrypt: KMS AccessDenied. Curious thing: CloudTrail shows the backup-service account activity, but no KMS Decrypt events around the same timestamp. Anyone seen this gap before?
encops-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-042. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-decrypt-fail 
kevin: Did we just rotate the CMK or change key policy last night? I remember an RBAC prune merged at 02:00.
sara: We did a housekeeping PR that renamed the backup uploader SA from `backup-runner` -> `backup-runner-v2` and removed a crufty role binding. It was supposed to be a no-op thanks to the grant proxy, but...
matt: If the SA name changed and we rely on serviceAccount-based grants in the KMS key policy, that would block decrypts. But weird that CloudTrail doesn't show KMS calls at all — implies the request never reached KMS or was blocked earlier.
dana: Also flagging vuln triage: devops found uploader v1 writes a temp file `/tmp/backup-cleartext-*` before upload. It's CVE-triage-worthy; we patched uploader in staging last week. Could be two correlated problems.
mira: Good catch on the temp files. For the current incident, the restore log shows:  `ERROR: unable to fetch CEK: AccessDenied` and upstream logs show 403 coming from our KMS proxy. No Retry attempts.
kevin: Quick checks — can someone run: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloudkms_key AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"backup-runner@redwood.iam\"" --limit 50` and also check CloudTrail/KMS logs for `Decrypt` entries for the CMK ID at 2026-03-23T02:03Z?
sara: ran the logging query — zero results for that principal during the window. There are admin events earlier but no decrypt. The backup-service did emit a signed request to our proxy though: `POST /v1/kms/decrypt` 403.
matt: That indicates our proxy rejected the request (RBAC layer) rather than KMS. Proxy uses an ephemeral grant mapping (svcacct -> key grant) that depends on IAM alias names. If alias changed, mapping returns 403 before calling KMS.
dana: For the vuln piece, ops already opened GH issue #9421 and a patch branch. I'll attach the minimal mitigation (tmpdir perms + immediate delete) to the incident so we don't lose track.
mira: Action items for now: 1) Recreate a temporary grant for `backup-runner-v2` to the CMK so restores can proceed. 2) Run a one-off decrypt test with the proxy using the broken SA token. 3) Add a CloudTrail/KMS forwarder policy to ensure we always retain decrypt events even when proxy denies.
encops-bot: Runbook step executed: created emergency temporary grant (10m). Restore attempt queued.
kevin: After emergency grant, restore succeeded for 2 of 3 shards. One failed with `timeout while fetching CEK` — likely race with grant propagation.
sara: Confirmed — final shard recovered after a second retry. We've left the temporary grant for 30m and scheduled a proper key-policy update.
matt: Post-incident follow-ups: update RBAC rename checklist to include: 1) KMS alias mapping audit, 2) pre-rotation decrypt smoke test, 3) add alert when a service account has auth logs but zero KMS decrypt events for backup ops.
dana: For the uploader vuln: short-term mitigation is to set `TMPDIR=/var/run/backup-tmp` with strict perms and delete on success. Long-term: switch to streaming ETL that never materializes full cleartext. I'll coordinate with platform.
mira: Also recommend we add explicit audit propagation: our proxy should log attempted principal and the denied KMS target, and forward that to SIEM as an 'kms_blocked' event. Right now denied proxy requests are only in proxy logs which aren't in the audit playbook.
encops-bot: Post-incident checklist created and assigned: @sara to update RBAC playbook, @dana to attach vuln PR and mitigation, @kevin to implement proxy audit forwarder. ETA 3 days.
mira: Thanks everyone. I'll capture notes for the incident review and we can schedule a short war-room Friday to validate the pre-rotation smoke test runs. :thumbsup:
